nipo.vintage_label: Global Trade Alert, New Industrial Policy Observatory, June 2026 extract (synthetic)
nipo.strength_words: Strength scores a measure by the bite of its instrument (a grant, loan, local-content rule or import ban counts more than monitoring), whether Global Trade Alert judges it to favour domestic firms, how widely it applies (a whole sector counts more than one named firm) and the money or trade it covers; measures that are part of a package of several instrument types count up to 60% more.
nipo.confidence_words: Mapping confidence says how firmly the measure's product list and text tie it to energy sectors (averaged over the sectors it maps to): 0.10 when none of its listed products are energy-sector goods, 0.25 for a measure without a product list, from 0.75 up when its products fall in these sectors, and up to 2 when its title, source and Global Trade Alert's sector flags corroborate the mapping.

pick.rule_d: its top upstream or midstream sector on the Strategic Index, leaving out geothermal and green hydrogen (excluded from allied picks by rule) and sectors with no recorded resource base

caveats.text: Scores compare Japan with other economies in the same sector; they are not measures of risk or profit in absolute terms.
All index values are the paper's baseline as of 12 October 2026; Strategic Insights recomputes them under other weightings.
Strategic Index scores within 0.01 of each other are almost tied: small changes in the data or the weights can swap their order.

Factory projects are cross-border solar, wind, battery and electric-vehicle manufacturing projects only, announced projects included, which may never be built; domestic investment is not covered (Cleantech Manufacturing FDI Dataset, edition 2026.10.05, CC BY 4.0; counts by the authors, a joint venture counted under its listed parent).
Where Japan or a partner did not report a flow, it is read from the other side's report, raised by 6% to value it like imports.
Some sectors have fewer than 10 economies with comparable scores, so their percentiles move in large steps.
Hong Kong's trade is largely re-exports.
Many allied picks are close calls: in the paper, 37% of them are within 0.01 of the runner-up.
Industrial-policy measures from the Global Trade Alert, New Industrial Policy Observatory, June 2026 extract (synthetic) are context only, outside the Policy index.
